intro: This is Halicarnassus, an ancient city in Muğla province whose story reaches back to the 11th century BC. It was the Carian capital, and here once stood the Mausoleum, one of the Seven Wonders.
history: Satrap Mausolus made this city his capital. When he died, his sister and wife Artemisia completed his colossal tomb. But it did not stand forever: earthquakes toppled it, and its stones were later quarried for the castle.
structure-1: You are now at the Mausoleum, one of the Seven Wonders and the building every mausoleum is named after. This was the tomb Artemisia, his sister and wife, raised for Mausolus, satrap of Caria. Picture it: a tall podium, thirty-six columns, a stepped pyramid, and on the summit a four-horse chariot.
structure-2: Here is the ancient theatre, carved into the hillside. It was the heart of the city's social and cultural life. Imagine the audience filling these seats.
structure-4: And now Bodrum Castle. This 15th-century fortress was built by the Knights of St John, and today it is home to a museum of underwater archaeology.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Myndos Gate.
facts: Did you know? The word 'mausoleum' comes directly from the name of Mausolus. In the fifteenth century the Knights Hospitaller quarried the Mausoleum and built its stone into Bodrum Castle. And Herodotus, the father of history, was born in this very city.
outro: This brings our tour of Halicarnassus to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
